subject: Unexpected priority-ingest charge on Nov 29 invoice - request for credit
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <agomez@brightlayer.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightLayer Billing <billing@brightlayer.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected priority-ingest charge on Nov 29 invoice

Hi Kimberly,

We just received November's invoice (INV-20261129-BL-77) and there is a ~USD 4,200 line item labeled 'ingest: priority processing (burst)'. We didn't enable any priority or expedited ingest settings on our side; last week our SREs did a large backfill but it should have been standard-priority.

Billing shows this as 2.1M tokens at the higher tier rate; this doesn't match our expectations. Can you help explain what triggered the priority flag and whether this is billable? If there's an internal misclassification we will ask for a credit. I've attached the BrightLayer billing summary and a small set of sample request ids/headers.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we're closing books next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of Engineering, BrightLayer
agomez@brightlayer.com

Attachment: brightlayer-ingest-sample-logs.json (sample request headers, timestamps, route ids)
Attachment: 2026-11-billing-summary.pdf (customer copy)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gomez <agomez@brightlayer.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:01:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected priority-ingest charge on Nov 29 invoice

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the logs. Looping in Ben (billing) and Marissa (account lead) so we can triage.

Quick note on process: priority-ingest is applied automatically when a request is routed to burst capacity pools (reserved fast-path GPUs) by our scheduler. That can happen when:

- The request has a priority flag from the customer API key (unlikely here), or
- Autoscaler detected sustained queue growth and temporarily routed to burst pools, or
- A manual ops escalation/pinning occurred for a route (rare).

Ben — can you confirm whether the Nov 29 cluster shift produced a burst billing event for BL-77 and whether those tokens were tagged as 'priority' in telemetry?

Marissa — can you confirm whether BrightLayer opened a ticket with support that might have triggered an ops pin?

We'll aim to get a first-pass explanation within 24 hours.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:37:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected priority-ingest charge on Nov 29 invoice

Kimberly — I pulled the telemetry and matched the sample request ids Alex provided. Notes:

- On 2026-11-29 02:12:00 UTC we had a short autoscaler window (approx 7 minutes) where the ingest queue for region-us-spoke-3 doubled due to a backlog from a downstream ETL job. The scheduler chose to route older queued items to the burst pool (priority path) to avoid latency SLO violations.
- Those requests were tagged in our billing pipeline as priority-ingest because the execution ran on reserved burst nodes; total billed tokens for that window = 2,134,820 tokens.
- I do see one anomalous attribution: ~18% of tokens in that window were from long-running batched backfills that our KV-prefix caching should have deduplicated. The dedup/cache miss rate was higher than expected because the backfill used a slightly different request signature (extra metadata param).

Given the above, I recommend: 1) offer a partial credit for the cached-eligible tokens (~18% => ~$760), and 2) classify the remaining burst routing as valid per our SLA (we auto-route to protect latency).

I can prepare an evidence pack (sample logs, node assignment, billing tags) if we want to push a larger goodwill credit.

Ben
Billing Lead, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-evidence-window-20261129.tar.gz (billing tags & node assignment CSV)
From: Alex Gomez <agomez@brightlayer.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightLayer Billing <billing@brightlayer.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected priority-ingest charge on Nov 29 invoice

Thanks for the fast investigation and the breakdown. The proposed partial credit sounds reasonable — BrightLayer is willing to accept the partial credit for the cache-eligible portion, but we also want a one-time waiver for the ops routing since the backfill was internal (triggered by our ETL batch) and the burst had material downstream cost impact on our P&L.

Two asks before we close the loop:
1) Can you provide the preserved sample logs and the mapping from request-id -> node-id so our engineering team can confirm request signatures? (we saw the metadata param mismatch)
2) Can Redwood add a guard to prevent autoscaler from routing background backfills to priority pools for customers who opt-out? We'd like a setting at the project/account level.

If we can get the logs + confirmation of the partial credit and an account-level opt-out timeline, we'll approve the credit and settle the invoice immediately.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex Gomez
Head of Engineering, BrightLayer
